source_caption_text:
Bro had no business going this crazy in 20 seconds

DaeMoney, Veeze and LUCKI link up on “GTA,” but LUCKI’s verse is the part that really stands out. He slides onto the beat with that laid-back, slurred delivery that makes everything sound effortless, barely changing his tone while still making every line hit.

The crazy part is how quickly he makes his presence felt. His verse is short, but the way he glides over the beat fits the track perfectly. LUCKI doesn’t need to do too much or switch up his flow to grab your attention. He just gets on the beat and does his thing.

That’s what makes LUCKI’s features so memorable. Even when he only gets a few bars, he has a way of making you want to rewind and run the verse back. His appearance on “GTA” is another example of how he can slide on a track like he’s barely trying and still leave one of the biggest impressions.
